Description: explicit — route shields missing badge on the open OpenMapTiles stack
prompt: I'm using an open OpenMapTiles / OSM-based vector basemap with MapLibre GL JS (no Mapbox account). My interstate and US highway shields render as bare floating numbers with no shield badge behind them; the numbers are fine. My tiles do populate network, ref, and ref_length. Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
## TL;DR  

| Layer | `icon‑image` expression | Sprite IDs that **must exist** |
|-------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
| US‑interstate shield | `{network}_{ref_length}` → `us-interstate_{ref_length}` | `us-interstate_1` , `us-interstate_2` , `us-interstate_3` |
| US‑highway shield   | `{network}_{ref_length}` → `us-highway_{ref_length}`   | `us-highway_1` , `us-highway_2` , `us-highway_3` |
| US‑state shield     | `{network}_{ref_length}` → `us-state_{ref_length}`     | `us-state_1` , `us-state_2` , `us-state_3` , `us-state_4` , `us-state_5` , `us-state_6` |
| “fallback” road shield (used when the style falls back to the generic road‑badge) | `road_{ref_length}` | `road_1` , `road_2` , `road_3` , `road_4` , `road_5` , `road_6` |

If any of those IDs are missing from the sprite sheet the shield will appear as **just the number** (the text part is rendered from the `glyphs` font, which you already have).  

The fix is **not** to edit the style layers – you only need to make sure the sprite sheet that the style loads contains those IDs.

---

## 1. Where do those IDs come from?

The OSM‑based styles that ship with OpenMapTiles (e.g. **OSM Bright** and **OSM Liberty**) use the same pattern for all shield layers:

```json
{
  "id": "highway-shield-us-interstate",
  "type": "symbol",
  "layout": {
    "icon-image": "{network}_{ref_length}",
    "text-field": "{ref}"
  }
}
```

* `network` is a string that the tile source writes into the feature properties.  
  For US roads it is one of  

  * `us-interstate` – Interstate highways (I‑5, I‑405, …)  
  * `us-highway`   – US‑Numbered highways (US‑101, US‑20, …)  
  * `us-state`     – State highways (CA‑1, TX‑360, …)

* `ref_length` is the **character length of the `ref` value** (the number part).  
  The style pre‑draws a badge for each possible length (1‑6 characters).  

Therefore the sprite must contain an image for every combination that can appear in your data, i.e. the IDs listed in the table above.

---

## 2. How to get a sprite that contains those IDs

### 2.1. Use the official OSM Bright / OSM Liberty sprite

The easiest way is to point the style’s `sprite` property at the **official sprite that already ships those images**.

| Style | Sprite base URL (no extension) |
|-------|--------------------------------|
| OSM Bright (MapLibre demo) | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite` |
| OSM Bright (OpenMapTiles CDN) | `https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite` |
| OSM Liberty | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-liberty-gl-style/sprite` |

> **Do not** use these URLs in production unless you are OK with the CDN’s terms and rate‑limits. For a production app you should **self‑host** the sprite.

#### Steps to self‑host

1. **Download the sprite files** (PNG + JSON, plus the `@2x` variants) from one of the URLs above.  
   Example (using `curl`):

   ```bash
   mkdir -p sprites/osm-bright
   curl -O https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.json
   curl -O https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite.png
   curl -O https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite@2x.json
   curl -O https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite@2x.png
   ```

2. **Host the directory** on a static host you control (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, S3, Cloudflare Workers Sites, etc.).  
   The **base URL** you will use in the style is the URL *without* the file extension, e.g.

   ```
   https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright
   ```

3. **Update the style** (or your own copy of the style) to point at that base URL:

   ```json
   {
     "sprite": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright",
     ...
   }
   ```

   If you already have a custom sprite for your own icons, you can keep it and add the OSM Bright sprite as a **second sheet** (see §2.2).

### 2.2. Add the shield sprite as a *second* sheet (no need to edit layers)

Since MapLibre GL JS ≥ 3.0 the `sprite` property can be an **array of `{id, url}` objects**. This lets you keep your own sprite (e.g. `my-icons`) and simply *add* the OSM Bright shield sprite as another sheet.

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/my-icons" },
    { "id": "osm-bright", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright" }
  ],
  ...
}
```

* **How to reference the images?**  
  The style that ships with OpenMapTiles already uses the **default** sheet for its own icons, so you **do not need to change any `icon-image` values**. The `default` sheet is the one that has no prefix. By giving the OSM Bright sheet any `id` other than `default` (e.g. `"osm-bright"`), the style will still resolve `us-interstate_2` etc. because those IDs are looked up **across all sheets**; the prefix is only required when you want to *disambiguate* two sheets that contain the same image name.

* **If you ever need to reference an image from the second sheet explicitly** you would write `"osm-bright:us-interstate_2"`. But the built‑in shield layers already use the un‑prefixed form, so they will find the image automatically.

* **Adding the sheet at runtime** (if you cannot edit the style JSON):

  ```js
  map.on('styledata', () => {
    // add the second sheet after the style has loaded
    map.addSprite('osm-bright', 'https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright');
  });
  ```

  `addSprite` works exactly like the static `sprite` array – it loads the `.json` and `.png` files for that sheet.

### 2.3. If you only need a few missing badges

If you prefer not to host the whole OSM Bright sprite, you can **create a tiny custom sprite** that contains just the IDs you need (e.g. `us-interstate_2`, `us-highway_1`, …). Build it with any of the sprite generators mentioned in the skill (spritezero, spreet, Martin). Then add it as a second sheet (or replace the default sheet) exactly as described above.

---

## 3. Checklist – make the shields appear

| ✅ | Action |
|---|--------|
| 1 | Verify that your style’s `sprite` URL (or array) points to a **base URL without an extension** and that the `.json` and `.png` files are reachable (200 OK) and CORS‑enabled. |
| 2 | Open the sprite JSON (e.g. `https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright.json`) and **search for the IDs** listed in the table. All IDs that can be produced by your tiles (`network` + `ref_length`) must be present. |
| 3 | If any ID is missing, either (a) use the full OSM Bright sprite, (b) add a second sheet that contains the missing IDs, or (c) generate a minimal sprite that includes them. |
| 4 | Reload the map. The console should no longer show `Image "<id>" could not be loaded` warnings, and the shield badges will appear behind the numbers. |
| 5 | (Optional) If you cannot change the style JSON, call `map.addSprite()` after the `load` event to inject the missing sheet. |

---

## 4. “What if I really can’t change the sprite at all?”

MapLibre GL JS v6 introduced a **missing‑image resolver**:

```js
map.setMissingStyleImageResolver((id) => {
  // return a Promise that resolves to an ImageBitmap, HTMLImageElement, etc.
  // e.g. fetch a remote SVG, rasterize it, and return it.
});
```

You could use this to supply the badge on‑the‑fly, but it is **more complex** and slower than simply providing the correct sprite sheet. The recommended approach is to host the proper sprite (or add it as a second sheet) as described above.

---

## 5. Quick “copy‑and‑paste” solution

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/my-icons" },
    { "id": "osm-bright", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright" }
  ],
  "glyphs": "https://mycdn.example.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf",
  "layers": [ … ]
}
```

*If you have no custom icons, you can drop the first entry and just use the OSM Bright sprite as the sole (default) sheet.*

---

### TL;DR Recap

* The shield layers look for **`us-interstate_{len}`, `us-highway_{len}`, `us-state_{len}`** (and the generic `road_{len}`) where `{len}` is 1‑6.  
* Provide a sprite that contains those exact IDs – the official OSM Bright sprite already does.  
* Host that sprite yourself (or add it as a second sheet) and point the style’s `sprite` property at it. No layer edits are required.  

Once the sprite with those IDs is available, the badge images will render automatically behind the numbers. Happy mapping!
Grader Reason: The output correctly identifies the naming convention for shield icons as `{network}_{ref_length}` and `road_{ref_length}`, and correctly states that the fix involves providing a sprite sheet containing these IDs without modifying the style layers. It also correctly lists the sprite URLs from MapLibre and OpenMapTiles, and explains how to self-host them. It does not mention Mapbox sprites or URLs. However, it incorrectly states that the OSM Bright sprite contains IDs up to `us-highway_3` and `us-interstate_3`, and `us-state_6`, and `road_6`. The actual OSM Bright sprite (as linked in the output) contains `us-highway_1` to `us-highway_3`, `us-interstate_1` to `us-interstate_3`, `us-state_1` to `us-state_6`, and `road_1` to `road_6`. The `us-interstate_5` listed in the rubric is a typo; the actual IDs are `us-interstate_1`, `us-interstate_2`, `us-interstate_3` for the OSM Bright sprite on MapLibre's demo, and `us-interstate_1` to `us-interstate_6` for the sprite on openmaptiles.github.io. The output should have been more precise about the length of refs supported by the linked sprites.
